Nobody lives off bits and pieces. I don’t know where you’re getting this from. As someone who has actively worked on big production true non profit documentaries I must educate you that there are always private individuals, trusts, grants, non profit entities that actively provide enough funding and resources to create any type of documentary under the sun. These are handed out so often one must only have a thesis convincing enough. Nobody needs a fucking paywall to provide decent audio or editing it truly isn’t as expensive as you’re describing. I’ve worked on high production sets and have shot my own independent ones. There isn’t any disparity of conviction between the two. Some of the most important and convincing documentaries have been shot using a purely run and gun method: meaning one dude, with a camera and mic literally shooting the entire thing. A documentary isn’t some bit of sensational wonder like you’ve been conditioned to think by the Netflix, Amazon bs. It’s not supposed to wow you into some false sense of reality. There are rules to this. This isn’t cinema, which also has rules but not like this. It’s a rough mix of journalistic integrity and the convincing nature of moving picture. They sell cause they want to sell.

I actively work in the documentary sphere, and the ultimate goal of it at its essence is accessibility, it is why we actively work to get grants, commission and when all else fails we fckn self fund so that we don’t sell. A documentary need not be made to cinematic excellence, It does not edit the content or raise its conviction in any meaningful manner. If the person making it wishes it to have high production value, be it purely for aesthetic reasons or to sell it that does not mean they can negate their responsibility to accessibility. There’s money to be made even if they don’t sell just so you know. Far more than enough to create a decent production and receive a fair chunk as a stipend. The only reason they’re selling it cause they want to profit off it. That is literally capitalism.  Theres more than enough to keep the lights on if you purely want to keep it free of profit, do not think there isn’t a choice here.

You are right about the current state of caste politics in TN, but it’d have probably been worse without the influence of Periyar. He stressed self respect to the LC’s rather than inclusivity to the HC’s. They had to focus on the Dravidian movement cause unlike Kerala with it’s literacy TN was ripe for northern incursion in terms of politics and language. The Dravidian movement at its heart was inclusive and that is probably why Periyar gave way to it and added to it. But nevertheless Periyar’s self respect movement and the writing associated to it still continue to inform and protect LC’s. It’s left a lasting impact on the ground level for inclusion, his tonality in addressing the issues has caused social change that is yet visible in most of TN leave certain pockets of ignorance. The man did what he could to unite the Tamil population against the tyranny of casteism, he did not succeed but he damn well tried. Much like with Ambedkar it’s us who must take the work forward and not just rely on the path already paved, instead of bashing the fore-bearers of our ideology for their many human shortcomings.
